meta.notes: Evidence is mostly pro forums (Thumbtack Community, windowcleaner.com), platform help pages, FTC coverage and vendor/agency pages; complaint bias is strong. Many sources were unfetchable for Preuve (BBB, Trustpilot, FTC.gov, Jobber help, HomeAdvisor help, Alignable, G2) and were not cited. Tack Tools Pro (a Thumbtack lead-response tool with a 'Fair Credit' refund-drafting feature, reported launched 2026) surfaced in search but its press release was not readable, so it is mentioned in the report only, not cited. Prospects: 19 companies (short of the 20 target); Thumbtack/Angi profile pages are not fetchable, so only companies' own sites were used; several have only first-name owners and most lack size data. No people's names are used in evidence except contacts printed on companies' own pages.

summary.statement: Pros report that lead-to-hire and spend-to-revenue ratios are not available from Thumbtack and only become visible after months.
Marketplace leads are described as hard to attribute because the platform controls the customer interaction.
Where tracking happens it is manual: owner math, spreadsheets or templates where staff log the source.
Housecall Pro's ROI table already reports cost per job by source including Thumbtack and Angi, but it depends on manually entered spend and filled lead-source fields.
Shared leads are structural: Angi may match a request with up to five pros, and pros report leads going to 3-4 competitors.
Pros describe bursts of bot/fake leads and 'dozens' of dead leads; the FTC found HomeAdvisor overstated lead-to-job rates and sent off-service/out-of-area leads.
No source gives a representative rate of invalid leads; evidence is anecdotal and complaint-biased.
Refunds are manual, per-lead requests with conditions (Angi: under 45 days, call within 24h) and are paid as expiring account credits.
Pros report frequent denials and that fighting for credits is exhausting or not worth the time; some left platforms over it.
The refundable pool is narrow: unresponsive or shopping homeowners are explicitly not creditable on Angi or Thumbtack.
Platforms are automating credits themselves (Google LSA auto-credits; Thumbtack Fair Shot auto-refund) while also narrowing creditable reasons.
Individual pros report spend of $10k-$23k+ a year on Thumbtack and lead cost at 45-50% of resulting revenue.
Reported unrecovered waste ranges from a few hundred dollars a month to over $1,000 in a bot-lead burst.
Other pros report positive ROI (about 3x on Angi/HomeAdvisor), so waste is not universal.
Because most waste (no response, shopping, lost bids) is non-refundable, the claimable dollar amount per contractor is likely much smaller than total 'wasted' spend.
Housecall Pro and Jobber both have lead-source fields; Housecall Pro has a marketing ROI table with spend and cost per job by source.
These depend on manual spend entry and consistent source tagging, which is often incomplete.
Some solo pros use client software with automated invoicing, but how many target-ICP pros use any FSM was not found.

competitors.description: Native credit request flow for invalid contact info, wrong location, service mismatch, duplicates and paused-lead charges.

sentiment.statement: A contractor says HomeAdvisor rejected countless credit requests even for disconnected numbers.

competitors.name: Contractor marketing agencies (e.g. Hook Agency)
competitors.description: Agencies pitch owned channels (SEO, LSA) as the way out of shared marketplace leads.

current_solutions.statement: Most pros track lead-source ROI manually (owner math, spreadsheets, templates) or not at all.
FSMs like Housecall Pro and Jobber already offer lead-source reporting, with Housecall Pro showing cost per job by source, but rely on manual spend entry and tagging.
Refunds are claimed one by one through each platform's own flow, and platforms are increasingly automating credits themselves.
Some pros respond by leaving marketplaces for owned channels, often with agency help.
